title: Earth: The Only Planet With Pizza (and You!)
summary: What's the one thing that makes Earth totally unique in the solar system? It's not the mountains or the oceans. It's you. Earth is the only planet known to have life — from microscopic amoebas to submarine-size blue whales to a kid reading this right now. Earth sits third from the sun, about 93 million miles away. Its average temperature is a comfortable 59°F (15°C). That's just right for liquid water, which other planets don't have. Our atmosphere — the layer of air around us — does two big jobs. It gives us breathable air, and it acts like a force field. Every day, as much as 22 million pounds of meteors burn up harmlessly in our atmosphere. That's like 5,000 school buses of space rocks, gone in a flash! Life began in Earth's oceans more than 3.5 billion years ago. Those oceans cover nearly 70 percent of the planet. Here's a wild fact: scientists know more about the surface of the moon than they do about the deep parts of our own oceans. So there are still mysteries right here at home. Earth also has a tilt that gives us seasons. Near the poles, some spots get 24 hours of daylight or darkness. And our planet's molten core creates a magnetic field that shields us from solar radiation and makes auroras — amazing light shows in the sky. Even the land moves! The continents creep about as fast as your fingernails grow. So the next time you look up at the stars, remember: you're already on the coolest planet around.
why_it_matters: It reminds you that the planet you live on is doing amazing things for you every single day — and that some of the best science mysteries are right under your feet or under the ocean.

background_read: Earth formed about 4.5 billion years ago, and it is still the only place we know of where life exists.
The air we breathe is mostly nitrogen and oxygen, and that same air protects us — small space rocks burn up before they can hit the ground.
Spacecraft have visited the Moon and other planets, but scientists say the deep oceans on Earth are still one of the least explored places anywhere.
Article_Structure: WHO: Earth, and everything living on it — from microscopic amoebas to blue whales to the kid reading this
WHAT: A look at what makes Earth the only known planet with life: liquid water, a protective atmosphere, a magnetic field, and just the right temperature
WHERE: Earth, the third planet from the sun, about 93 million miles away, with oceans covering nearly 70 percent of its surface
WHY: Earth's special features — the right warmth, breathable air, and a shield against solar radiation — keep life safe, and there are still mysteries right here at home

perspectives.description: They study Earth and other planets together, because comparing them shows exactly why our planet's air, water, and temperature let life thrive.
They point out that we know more about the Moon's surface than about the deep parts of our own oceans, so there is still a huge amount left to discover.
They see it as a reminder to take care of the planet that protects us — the atmosphere and oceans are what keep Earth the coolest place around.
